lius perseverantiæ circumscribuntur ab illis,
cùm inquiunt, in portis tuis. Testimonium verò
Ecclesiæ ad hæc omnia appellatur, quia illius
est testificari secundum Deū, tum de portis suis
(vt cum Propheta loquamur) tum de
membris intra portas eius agentibus.
Ac primus quidem ille locus de perseveran-
tia sanctorum nō temerè à piis adhibetur: quia
omnes homines ad sanctitatem veram à Deo
provocati & accensi in Ecclesia eius, adhuc ea
cæcitate mentis & carnis infirmitate sunt, dum
hic in terris vivunt & lubricū iter huius mundi
premunt, vt nullo fermè negotio pedes eorum
à viis quas Deus præscripsit avertantur. Probat
Deus, excæcat mundus, debilitat caro, pecca-

page.notes: Printed text runs from the top of the page to "siue" at the foot; "con-" is the catchword at the right. A dark stain or blot covers part of the word after "peccatum" ("tum...ngit"); the letters under it are unreadable, so I marked them as illegible. The left-hand edge shows the neighbouring page's show-through and was excluded. Handwritten marks in the top right margin were excluded. Printed "s" forms were normalised to plain s, and the italic phrases were marked. The word "pedes" (after "cùm sibi") is partly obscured by the fold in the printed line; it reads clearly enough, but the line "cùm sibi pe-des" was joined across the hyphen as printed.
